name: Kenya
sources: GDP $8.6bn and 23.4m people (World Bank, 1990). The August 1989 census counted 21.4m; 23.4m is the World Bank mid-1990 estimate on a 3.4% growth rate, among the highest recorded anywhere.
Inflation 15.7% (Central Bureau of Statistics Nairobi CPI, 1990); Central Bank of Kenya minimum lending rate around 19%, with the shilling on a crawling peg and a controlled foreign exchange regime.
Defence 2.3% of GDP: a small professional force built deliberately small after the 1982 Air Force coup attempt, with British and American training access at Nanyuki and Mombasa in exchange.

Public and publicly guaranteed debt 72% of GDP. Kenya was in a structural adjustment programme; the donors suspended balance-of-payments support in November 1991, which is a year and a half after the start date and is the pressure this number is meant to make reachable.

Stability 44 and authoritarianism 0.78: KANU had been the sole legal party since the 1982 section 2A amendment, candidate selection ran by queue-voting, and Robert Ouko, the foreign minister, was murdered in February 1990. The Saba Saba demonstrations of 7 July 1990 followed.
Separatism 0.15: the shifta legacy in the North Eastern Province and Somali irredentism there, plus majimbo agitation in the Rift Valley.
Military strength 4 for roughly 23,000 personnel and no expeditionary capability.
